results.title: Poor Cloudflare support - Feedback - Cloudflare Community
results.content:
The problem at hand originated from Cloudflare’s sudden decision to block parts of my website, supposedly due to the detection of phishing malicious code. What makes matters worse is the complete lack of prior warning or opportunity to address the alleged issue. Even though I acted promptly to check the problem as soon as I became aware of it and open a ticket to review, Cloudflare’s subsequent response has been disappointingly passive.

This prolonged delay has had real-world consequences, with frustrated customers contacting us daily, unable to access the site due to Cloudflare’s block and adding alarming modal warning about potential card details theft for phishing. This situation is deeply frustrating, especially considering our investment in Cloudflare’s Pro Plan. [...] As I navigate through this frustrating experience, I sincerely hope that no one else encounters a similar situation. The lack of communication and prolonged resolution process with Cloudflare has been immensely challenging, and I wouldn’t wish it upon anyone. It’s my fervent wish that Cloudflare addresses these issues promptly and efficiently for the benefit of all their users, ensuring a smoother experience for everyone in the future.

results.title: Cloudflare Wallets Launch With Spending Caps That Block ...
results.content: The underlying issue is dual: agents have no stable, persistent identity that merchants can recognize across sessions, and they have no machine-native way to pay for resources. Both problems make API onboarding — the gateway to almost every agentic capability — something agents cannot do independently. [...] The core problem it addresses is a business problem as much as a technical one: merchants who want to extend free-trial credits, referral bonuses, or personalized pricing to real customers cannot do so when agents have no persistent identity. An agent that re-registers with each API it calls cannot demonstrate it is acting on behalf of a legitimate organization; a spam agent and a legitimate enterprise researcher are indistinguishable from the merchant's perspective. The cloudflare.pay identity for agents concept solves this by linking wallet handles to a known Cloudflare account. [...] Cloudflare Wallets is a two-tier payment infrastructure for AI agents: an Account Wallet that humans control and fund with stablecoins, and Virtual Wallets that agents spend from within limits the Account Wallet owner sets. Right now, only wallet handle reservation is live — you can claim a human-readable identifier at cloudflare.pay, but the payment functionality (adding funds, issuing Virtual Wallets to agents, making purchases) is scheduled to arrive in the coming months. No specific date or geographic availability has been announced. The wallet pairs with Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway — announced July 1 — which lets websites and API operators charge agents per request; that product is also still in waitlist stage.
